coverage.r1: Roughly 14:53-20:30 is an all-English planning talk (AI tools, tests); 12:27-13:25, 20:31-30:23, 36:37-42:59 and 45:18-1:00:46 are Latin-transliterated, often garbled (e.g. 25:05-25:38 'ana bihna binkhales al-asal', 'ahana shay na'na' ma asal mufrad' could not be parsed into rows). 22:49-24:55 is a honey seller at the door (not Amal). Speaker labels are fragmented; many '?' lines were assigned from flow (e.g. 02:31 'or يتعلّم', 34:00 'هو بتيبست' self-fixed). The lesson is one long drill on بسّط/انبسط conjugations, so grammar rows dominate and vocab rows are few. Left out as S4 pronunciation: لقة/luka for لغة (00:39), بسّتني for بسطني (30:35), بيسبت for بيبسط (32:30), بنسبت for بنبسط (34:21), bansebet for banbeset (56:04), بيسبط for ببسّط (1:02:23), maruj for mahruj (22:09), 'ma' for ma3 (25:38, 26:19), stress on the T (55:25). Self-fixes not logged: أكتب→احكي (05:28), سميح→مبسوط (27:54), basati→basatini (41:09), بساتِتني→بساتِتك (35:58). English words inside Arabic not on her sheet, so not tier 3: software, research, possibility, test (she uses 'test' herself), mispronounce, AI. 26:19 'aswad' read as aswa2 = worse (on sheet), so not a vocab error.

English-only stretches: 11:00-20:30 (AI tooling discussion), 22:49-25:00 (beekeeper at the door), 45:39-49:57 (Renata / kiss-verb aside). S4 letter slips not written: لقة/luka 00:39, بسّتني 30:35, بنسبت 34:21, embasana 52:33, bansabet/ban sebet 56:04-56:12, بيسبط 1:01:34. No CHAT Amal lines in this transcript. Medi turn count = 110 Medi lines with Arabic script + ~70 Latin-transliterated Arabic lines.

r3_note: Diarization is badly fragmented (many '?:' lines, Amal/Medi labels swapped in places); I judged speaker from content. D5 is a mis-pairing by the compare step: r1's row inside D5 (26:38 akun -> 3am baseer) is the same row as D16, so D16 carries the grammar row and D5 is ruled only on r2's 26:19 'aswad' vocab question. The 26:19 Latin transcript cannot show a final hamza (aswad 'black' vs aswa2 'worse'), so D5 is kept low. D18 turns on a doubled t (basato vs basatto) that the Latin transliteration cannot encode and Amal echoed without a fix, so it is dropped as unverifiable rather than as 'not an error'. Several r2/r1 rows in the 30:00-52:00 conjugation drill are letter-order slips (بيسبت for بيبسط, embasana for embasatna) that the READER-BRIEF explicitly classes as S4; I dropped those (D8, D10, D12, D17, D20). D14 (بتحمس -> متحمس, B15) is a separate moment from the 03:43 بهمس -> بتحمس fix and should not be merged with it. 22:49-25:00 is a beekeeper interruption in English, not lesson content.

rows.medi_said: How do you say languages in it? Loka, lokat?
rows.why: He asked for the word for language(s); she supplied لغة (not on her sheet); his loka/luka is an S4 ق/غ slip.

rows.medi_said: يعني ،شو يعني شو لا-- what... What language?
rows.amal_said: No بلاقي، إنتا بتلاقي، شو لقيت؟
rows.why: She asked شو لقيت؟ twice (01:24, 01:31) and he decoded it as 'what language?' - he took لقيت for لغة, the word they had just been on at 00:57-01:03; she said 'No' and explained بلاقي / بتلاقي / لقيت (sheet: i found | Ana la2ait | أنا لقيت), so this is a wrong-word listening error, not a didn't-know: he never asked, he answered wrong and she corrected.
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same listening slip; tier 1 fits because he mapped her word onto a different lexical item (لغة) rather than asking for it, and her 'No' is an explicit-no, not an 'asked' signal. t=01:34 is the line that carries the wrong reading.

rows.medi_said: أنا لقيت الطريق منيح كتير

rows.english: I found a very good way / method.
rows.r3_why: Tier 1, not 2: طريق and طريقة are two different sheet entries with different meanings (road vs method), so he picked the wrong lexical item, not the wrong gender form of one noun.
